saints.name: St. Zephyrinus
saints.title: Pope
saints.shortBlurb: A pope of the early third century who guided the Roman Church through fierce doctrinal storms…
biography: A Roman by birth, Zephyrinus was bishop of Rome from 199 to 217, through the persecution of Septimius Severus, whose edict of 202 forbade conversion to Christianity under the severest penalties. He leaned heavily on his deacon Callixtus, whom he set over the public cemetery on the Appian Way that still bears that deacon's name; Callixtus would succeed him as pope.

His pontificate was tried by the Adoptionist sect of Theodotus the Tanner, condemned by his predecessor, and by the Monarchians, who so pressed the unity of God that they denied the distinction of Persons in the Trinity. A writer quoted by Eusebius honours him as a defender of the divinity of Christ; the scholar Hippolytus, in his Philosophumena, denounced him as an ignorant man governed by Callixtus.

He died on 20 December 217 and was buried in his own cemetery near that of Callixtus on the Appian Way. Long venerated as a martyr, his feast of 26 August was removed from the general calendar in 1969, for he had died a natural death; the Roman Martyrology now keeps his memory on 20 December.
saints.knownFor: Guiding the Roman Church amid early Trinitarian controversies.
